The non-ARPA years sit tightly around 17.6 to 19.1 million, while TY2021 under ARPA full refundability reached 37.771612 million. The announced conditional is a $1 earned-income threshold, not automatic full refundability, so TY2021 is an upper regime reference rather than the central base rate."},{"kind":"math","text":"Ladder: P(X <= 14) = 0.04; P(X <= 16) = 0.09; P(X <= 17.5) = 0.14; P(X <= 18.5) = 0.22; P(X <= 19.5) = 0.31; P(X <= 20.5) = 0.40; P(X <= 21.5) = 0.49; P(X <= 22.5) = 0.58; P(X <= 24) = 0.67; P(X <= 26) = 0.76; P(X <= 28.5) = 0.84; P(X <= 31.5) = 0.89; P(X <= 34) = 0.93; P(X <= 38) = 0.98. Linear interpolation gives the 10th percentile 16.300000 from call-0011, median 21.611111 from call-0012, and 90th percentile 32.125000 from call-0013."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence prior = recent non-ARPA level near 18.0 million; historical sample = 18.528360, 19.011027, 19.119249, 37.771612, 18.076696, 17.626084; adjustment components = judgmental policy-mechanism updates of +1.0 million for population and filing growth by TY2027, +2.5 million for families with very low earnings newly crossing the refundability threshold, and asymmetric upside for broader child-credit legislation bundled with the threshold. A formal trend or ARIMA-style prior is ruled out because the six-print history is dominated by statutory regime changes, so the operative prior is non-ARPA persistence plus stated policy adjustments. For the annual flow series I used the values themselves: sigma = 7.899 from call-0009, so 80% half-width check = 1.28*sigma = 10.111 from call-0010. The ladder-implied 80% width is 15.825 from call-0014, a 7.913 half-width, about 0.78x the 1.28*sigma check because TY2021 full refundability is more generous than the stated $1-threshold mechanism."},{"kind":"text","text":"Policy mechanism: lowering IRC §24(d)(1)(B)(i)'s earned-income threshold from the current-law threshold to no more than $1 mainly adds families with positive but very low earnings and increases marginal ACTC eligibility for some low earners. It does not by itself imply the TY2021 ARPA combination of full refundability, larger maximum credit, age-17 eligibility, and advance payment administration."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-considerations: upside risk is that enacted legislation paired with the $1 threshold also expands the refundable amount or child eligibility, which would land above the interval toward the TY2021 ARPA print. Downside risk is that take-up, qualifying-child counts, or very-low-earnings filing behavior remain close to current law, which would land near or below the lower interval. A materially different IRS Table 3.3 concept label or unresolved condition would be outside the interval as a scoring-state issue rather than a numeric miss."},{"kind":"text","text":"Review disposition: accepted the blocking resolver critique by preserving the structured thesis_announcement_fetch.fetch_official_announcement event for the exact registered URL and keeping resolutionDate at 2029-12-31. Accepted the model-prior warning by ruling out a formal trend prior, and accepted the update warning by labeling the +1.0 million and +2.5 million updates as judgmental policy-mechanism components rather than sourced estimates."},{"kind":"forecast","point":21.611111,"ciLow":16.3,"ciHigh":32.125}]}
